title: HistGramBench: Measuring Structural Recovery When Multimodal Models Redraw Historical Mathematical Diagrams as TikZ
abstract: arXiv:2611.00081v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Digital libraries preserve mathematical books printed from the sixteenth to the twentieth century, but the lettered diagrams in them, the figures on which Euclidean proofs depend, remain scanned images whose content cannot be searched. Redrawing such a diagram as a short drawing program would record which points lie on which lines and circles. But a printed plate offers no source code against which the redrawing could be checked. We introduce HistGramBench, a benchmark of 2,507 diagrams from 95 works printed between 1551 and 1933 in eight languages. translated_title: HistGramBench：衡量多模态模型将历史数学图形重绘为 TikZ 时的结构恢复能力
translated_abstract: 数字图书馆保存了十六至二十世纪印刷的数学著作，但其中的字母标注图形——即欧几里得证明所依赖的那些插图——仍然只是无法检索内容的扫描图像。将这样的图形重写为一段简短的绘图程序，可以记录下哪些点位于哪些直线或圆上。然而印刷版面并不提供可供核对的源代码。我们提出了 HistGramBench，一个包含1551年至1933年间以八种语言印刷的95部著作中2,507个图形的基准数据集。对于每个图形，由来自不同提供商的两个AI模型就读者从图中获取的事实（例如哪些线是平行的、两条线在哪里相交）达成一致，并且每次重绘都会在模型自己绘制的图形上依据这些事实进行核对。我们评估了六个价格可负担的AI模型，其中表现最好的恢复了约五分之三的事实，而模型遗漏的大部分来自程序……（原文摘要至此截断）
tldr: 提出 HistGramBench 基准，通过两个不同AI模型对历史数学图形中的几何事实达成共识来检验模型重绘的 TikZ 程序，发现最佳的平价模型也只能恢复约五分之三的结构事实。
en_tdlr: HistGramBench is a benchmark of 2,507 diagrams from 95 historical mathematical works (1551–1933) that verifies AI-generated TikZ redrawings against geometric facts agreed upon by two AI models from different providers, finding the best affordable model recovers only about three-fifths of these structural facts.
